- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting in early horizon, under-forecasting in late horizon; adjust downward in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0 point lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 15–20 days, reduce forecast slope; sentiment-driven corrections should be applied earlier (day 10–15).
